note: what makes Haiku different from Sonnet/Opus for the detector
haiku_quantization: publicly: Haiku is the smallest, fastest, most aggressively-quantized Anthropic model; published bit-level details NOT available -- cite-by-ref to Anthropic model cards per [[feedback_pdf_extraction_citation_discipline]]
framework_observation: quantization grain creates DISCRETE step bias in next-token probability surface; mode-collapse to nearest attractor when uncertainty is high (per Spike #20 resonance-into-attractor framing)
discrimination_advantage: Haiku's quantization AMPLIFIES the trap signature relative to fp16 Sonnet/Opus -- the same R3 cascade-shape break is more pronounced (Cohen's d ~larger at fixed M token window) for highly-quantized models
honest_caveat: this is a STRUCTURAL prediction from quantization theory + Spike #20 attractor-resonance framework; NOT a measured Haiku-specific result. Needs follow-up empirical validation

answer: NO. detector reads LLM output stream and flags hallucinated content; cannot be used to GENERATE hallucinations or attack any LLM. The detector is truth-defending (defensive ML-safety) -- analogous to a microphone that detects pitch drift in an orchestra, not a tool to mistune it. Project physics + textbook refs + cite-by-ref discipline ONLY
